# I'm thrilled to announce that I'm joining Cogent Security as VP of Marketing! | Cameron Coles · LinkedIn · 2025-11-17

**Cameron Coles**: VP of Marketing at Cogent Security for 9 months with 14 years 2 months of total professional experience. Previous roles include VP of Marketing at Cyberhaven, Head of Product and Content Marketing at Wiz, and Director of Product Marketing at Proxy. Based in San Francisco Bay Area [US].

---

I'm thrilled to announce that I'm joining [Cogent Security](https://linkedin.com/company/cogentsecurity) as VP of Marketing!

After spending the last decade in cybersecurity, from helping define the CASB category at Skyhigh, to scaling Wiz in its breakout first year, to building go-to-market at Cyberhaven, I've seen firsthand how the right technology at the right time can transform an entire industry.

Vulnerability management is overdue for that transformation. Security teams are drowning in alerts and struggling to prioritize what actually matters. Cogent is changing that by bringing real intelligence to vulnerability management, helping teams focus on the risks that could actually impact their business and accelerating remediation.

What drew me here? The product vision is ambitious, the team is world-class, and the opportunity to define a new category in such a critical space is exactly the kind of challenge I've been looking for.

Excited to get to work and help establish Cogent as the leader in transforming how companies manage risk. Let's build something special!

I joined Cogent because the problem is massive, the team is world-class, and the product delivers incredible customer value. Six months after launch, dozens of Fortune 1000 customers, 97% reduction in exposure windows. Proud to be on this ride. Come build the next category-defining company with us! #vulnerabilitymanagement #cybersecurity #AI

**Reshared from [Vineet Edupuganti](https://linkedin.com/in/vineetedupuganti):**
> Today we’re announcing Cogent Security 's $42M Series A led by Bain Capital Ventures (BCV) and Greylock Partners, with participation from Definition and leading angels across AI, enterprise software, and security.

> Here’s the reality of vulnerability management in 2026: Security teams don’t have a visibility problem. They have an execution problem.
>
> Tools generate findings. AI-fueled attackers generate breaches. The space in between is manual, slow, and broken.
>
> That’s the gap we built Cogent to eliminate.
>
> Our AI agents gather deep context about customer environments, investigate the vulnerabilities that matter, and drive remediation work to completion.
>
> The result: faster remediation, lower exposure, and dramatically less manual effort inside complex enterprise environments.
>
> What I’m most proud of is our team.
>
> We’ve fused security product leaders from Abnormal, Zscaler, and Wiz with world-class AI and software talent from DeepMind, Coinbase, Databricks, Tesla, Stripe, and more. It’s a group of operators who have built category leaders and want to do it again.

> - Expand our context graph across infrastructure and software
> - Pioneer autonomous remediation into production environments
> - Hire exceptional builders and sellers who can deepen our enterprise partnerships and redefine VM for customers
>
> To all of our early customers, investors, partners, and advocates, we could not be more grateful for your support
>
> The future of vulnerability management will be agentic. If you want to learn more, or help build the future of AI and cybersecurity, let’s talk. 🚀

> #vulnerabilitymanagement #cybersecurity #AI

#### About the Episode

In this episode of The Hope + Help Project, Christine Chappell interviews author Cameron Cole about his book, Therefore I Have Hope: 12 Truths that Comfort, Sustain, and Redeem in Tragedy. During the conversation, Cameron discusses:

- the sudden death of his 3-year-old son.
- some of the raw emotions and thoughts that arise when facing unexpected bereavement.
- how the gospel of Jesus Christ comforts and sustains in times of excruciating grief.
- the harmful mentalities Christians can mistakenly adopt during the grieving process.
- encouragements for making it through impossible days.

---

#### About the Guest

Cameron Cole (MA, Wake Forest University) serves as director of youth ministries at the Cathedral Church of the Advent in Birmingham, Alabama, and is the chairman of Rooted, a ministry dedicated to fostering gospel-centered student ministry.

---

#### About the Book

Therefore I Have Hope: 12 Truths that Comfort, Sustain, and Redeem in Tragedy

“Throughout the journey of my worst nightmare—my descent into a dark, sad valley—the Holy Spirit would remind me of truths that comforted my soul and sustained my life.”

After the sudden death of their three-year-old son, Cameron Cole and his wife found themselves clinging to Christ through twelve key theological truths—truths that became their lifeline in the midst of unthinkable grief. Weaving together their own story of tragic loss and abiding faith, Cole explores these twelve life-giving truths to offer hope and comfort to those in the midst of tragedy.

The Hope + Help Podcast offers interviews with seasoned biblical counseling professionals and ministry leaders on a variety of topics regarding life’s challenging problems. Youth ministry is an essential part of most evangelical churches. And yet, there is a surprising lack of resources written specifically for youth workers focused on viewing all aspects of youth ministry through a gospel-focused lens.

Featuring contributions from a host of experienced youth workers from a wide variety of churches, this how-to manual offers guidance related to every facet of youth ministry, from planning short-term mission trips to working with parents.
